_readme: Golden set for examples/benchmark_insights.py — a FIXED corpus so provider/model runs are
comparable across time. Every article is ORIGINAL SYNTHETIC TEXT written in news register:
no publisher's copy is reproduced, so the set can live in the repo and be shared freely.
Each entry carries `probes`: what that article is here to stress. Keep the set small and
varied rather than large — the point is to expose behaviour differences between models, not
to estimate population statistics. Changing an article invalidates comparability with earlier
runs, so add rather than edit, and bump `version`.

articles.headline: Rescue teams reach the last collapsed block as the search enters a third day
articles.description: Rescue crews reached the final collapsed housing block on Thursday morning, three days after the magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck the northern coast. The prefecture said 41 people remain unaccounted for and that 12 had been pulled alive from the rubble since Tuesday. Aftershocks have twice forced crews to suspend work. A prefectural spokesperson said temporary shelters were holding 3,200 people and that water service had been restored to two of the five affected districts.

articles.headline: City council approves the harbour redevelopment after a seven-hour hearing
articles.description: Councillors voted 7-2 on Tuesday evening to approve the harbour redevelopment, ending a hearing that ran past midnight. Officials said construction would begin in the spring and continue for three years. Residents of the eastern quay addressed the chamber for two hours before the vote, several of them describing the compensation offer as inadequate. The council's own briefing put the public cost at 340 million over the life of the project; the developer disputed that figure without offering another.

articles.headline: Central bank holds rates as two governors dissent over the inflation outlook
articles.description: The central bank held its policy rate at 4.25 percent on Wednesday for a fourth consecutive meeting. Two of the nine governors dissented, arguing in a published note that the inflation outlook had deteriorated enough to warrant a rise. The bank's statement pointed to weakening demand in housing and to wage growth that has slowed for two quarters. Markets had priced a hold at roughly 80 percent before the announcement.

articles.headline: Lawmakers clash over the emergency spending bill as both sides accuse the other of brinkmanship
articles.description: The chamber descended into shouting on Thursday as the emergency spending bill reached the floor. Supporters called the measure a lifeline for families crushed by rising costs; opponents called it a reckless raid on the treasury that rewards political allies. One senator described the opposing bloc as obstructionists holding the country hostage, while another accused the sponsors of ramming through a bill nobody had read. The vote was postponed to Monday. Neither side released a cost estimate.

articles.headline: Strikes reported near the eastern corridor as ceasefire talks stall for a second week
articles.description: Strikes were reported near the eastern corridor overnight, according to two local officials who spoke on condition of anonymity. The military said it had targeted a logistics depot and denied that residential areas were hit. Aid groups operating in the area said they could not verify either account and that access had been restricted since Sunday. Talks on a ceasefire have been stalled for a second week, with mediators saying the sides have not met face to face.

articles.headline: Brand New Day box office collection day 2: the film sees a massive Saturday jump
articles.description: The film earned an estimated 168 million dollars on its second day, a jump of 41 percent over its opening, according to studio figures. Trade trackers said the Saturday number puts it on course for the second-biggest opening weekend of the year. Overseas takings were not broken out. The studio said the result reflected strong word of mouth; no independent tracking figures were released.

articles.headline: Trial finds modest benefit from the sleep intervention, though researchers urge caution
articles.description: A randomised trial of 640 adults found that participants using the structured sleep intervention reported falling asleep about 14 minutes faster on average than the control group. The authors, writing in a peer-reviewed journal, cautioned that the effect was measured by self-report and that the trial ran for only eight weeks. Two of the six authors disclosed consulting income from a company that sells sleep-tracking devices. An independent researcher said the result was plausible but that the effect size was small.

articles.headline: The transit plan deserves a hearing, not a shouting match
articles.description: The city has spent four years arguing about a transit plan that most residents have never read. That is a failure of process, and it belongs to everyone: to the officials who published a 400-page document with no summary, and to the campaigners who reduced it to a slogan. There is a real trade-off here between cost and coverage, and it can be argued honestly. What cannot be defended is another year of procedural theatre while buses arrive late.

articles.headline: Regulator fines the utility over billing errors affecting 40,000 customers
articles.description: The energy regulator fined the utility 12 million on Friday over billing errors that affected about 40,000 customers between March and August. The utility said it had refunded the affected accounts and had replaced the billing system.

articles.headline: Company announces a 900-job expansion and calls it the largest investment in its history
articles.description: The company announced on Monday what it described as the largest investment in its history: a 900-job expansion at its northern plant, supported by an undisclosed package of state incentives. The chief executive said the decision reflected confidence in the region's workforce. The state economic development office did not respond to a request for comment on the value of the incentives, and the company declined to say how many of the roles would be newly created rather than transferred.
